rot.means.ideia.ex1.e1: This pawn's key squares are b6, c6 and d6. Until now, the way to them was the opposition; but the opposition is a means, and the goal is the key square.
rot.means.ideia.ex1.livre.fala: Keep playing as White and see how Black defends.
rot.means.ideia.ex1.livre.volta: Let's go back to the starting position. Suggest another move or click {verResposta}
rot.means.ideia.ex1.fins.capturado: The black king captured the pawn.
rot.means.ideia.ex1.fins.repeticao: The black king always blocks the way.
rot.means.ideia.ex1.fins.limite: The black king always blocks the way.
rot.means.ideia.ex1.p: White to move. Think and suggest a move, or click {verResposta}
rot.means.ideia.ex1.certo: Your king goes straight next to the key squares.
rot.means.ideia.ex1.revela: The best is to take the king to c5, next to b6, c6 and d6, even without the opposition.
rot.means.ideia.ex1.err.d4e3.1: After this move, White no longer wins: Black can draw.
rot.means.ideia.ex1.err.d4e3.2: The black king goes to d7, next to c6 and d6. Your king stepped back and can no longer reach the key squares in time.
rot.means.ideia.ex1.err.d4e4.1: By taking the king to e4, you take the direct opposition, but White no longer wins: Black draws.
rot.means.ideia.ex1.err.d4e4.2: The black king goes to d6, one of the key squares, and blocks your king's path.
rot.means.ideia.ex1.err.d4d3.1: After this move, White no longer wins: Black can draw.
rot.means.ideia.ex1.err.d4d3.2: The black king goes to d6, one of the key squares, and blocks your king's path.
rot.means.ideia.ex1.err.d4c3.1: After this move, White no longer wins: Black can draw.
rot.means.ideia.ex1.err.d4c3.2: The black king goes to d6, one of the key squares, and blocks your king's path.
rot.means.ideia.ex1.err.c4c5.1: After this move, White no longer wins: Black can draw.
rot.means.ideia.ex1.err.c4c5.2: The black king goes to d7, next to c6, and gets in front of the pawn in time.
rot.means.ideia.ex1.l.1: Your king is on c5, next to the three key squares, and the kings are not facing each other: nobody has the opposition. But the black king cannot guard all three at once.
rot.means.ideia.ex1.l.3: Black takes the king to d7, to guard c6 and d6.
rot.means.ideia.ex1.l.4: You go to b6, the key square that was left free.
rot.means.ideia.ex1.l.5: The black king goes to c8, in front of the pawn.
rot.means.ideia.ex1.l.6: Your king goes to c6 and controls b7, c7 and d7. The black king only has the eighth rank.
rot.means.ideia.ex1.l.7: The black king goes to b8, next to c8.
rot.means.ideia.ex1.l.8: Your king goes to d7 and controls c8. Now the pawn advances on its own and promotes.
rot.means.ideia.ex1.l.9: Now compare it with the move that wins the direct opposition: the king on e4.
rot.means.ideia.ex1.l.10: Your king faces the black king, with one square between them. You have the opposition.
rot.means.ideia.ex1.l.11: But the black king goes to d6, a key square, and blocks the way. White no longer wins.
rot.means.ideia.ex1.l.12: Having the opposition did not help: it left d6 free for the black king. Near the key squares, take the king straight to them. Now the defence: the black king also thinks of the goal first.
rot.means.ideia.ex2.e1: Now from Black's side. With the pawn on c3, the key squares are b5, c5 and d5, and the white king, on e5, is already next to d5: your king must guard all three.
rot.means.ideia.ex2.livre.fala: Keep playing as Black and see how White attacks.
rot.means.ideia.ex2.livre.volta: Let's go back to the starting position. Suggest another move or click {verResposta}
rot.means.ideia.ex2.fins.afogado: Your king was stalemated: it is a draw.
rot.means.ideia.ex2.fins.repeticao: The white king did not get through.
rot.means.ideia.ex2.fins.limite: The white king did not get through.
rot.means.ideia.ex2.p: Black to move. Think and suggest a move, or click {verResposta}
rot.means.ideia.ex2.certo: On c6, your king guards b5, c5 and d5.
rot.means.ideia.ex2.revela: The best is to take the king to c6, next to all three key squares.
rot.means.ideia.ex2.err.d7e7.1: By taking the king to e7, you keep the opposition, but White can win.
rot.means.ideia.ex2.err.d7e7.2: The white king goes to d5, a key square of the pawn. With the king on it, the pawn promotes.
rot.means.ideia.ex2.err.d7c7.1: After this move, White can win.
rot.means.ideia.ex2.err.d7c7.2: The white king goes to d5, a key square of the pawn. With the king on it, the pawn promotes.
rot.means.ideia.ex2.err.d7c8.1: After this move, White can win.
rot.means.ideia.ex2.err.d7c8.2: The white king goes to d5, a key square of the pawn. With the king on it, the pawn promotes.
rot.means.ideia.ex2.err.d7d8.1: After this move, White can win.
rot.means.ideia.ex2.err.d7d8.2: The white king goes to d5, a key square of the pawn. With the king on it, the pawn promotes.
rot.means.ideia.ex2.err.d7e8.1: After this move, White can win.
rot.means.ideia.ex2.err.d7e8.2: The white king goes to d5, a key square of the pawn. With the king on it, the pawn promotes.
rot.means.ideia.ex2.l.1: On c6, your king guards the three key squares without facing the white king.
rot.means.ideia.ex2.l.2: The white king goes to d4, still next to c5 and d5.
rot.means.ideia.ex2.l.3: You face him on d6 and guard c5 and d5. If the white king goes to c4, heading for b5, the opposition lets your king go to c6 and guard b5 too.
rot.means.ideia.ex2.l.4: White pushes the pawn to c4. The key squares become b6, c6 and d6.
rot.means.ideia.ex2.l.5: Your king goes to c6, in front of the pawn, and Black draws.
rot.means.ideia.ex2.l.6: Remember: in defence, the goal is to guard the key squares. The opposition is only worth something if it helps with that.
rot.means.demos.erroDefesa.1: Again with White: the black king took the opposition on e7, but it does not guard d5, a key square.
rot.means.demos.erroDefesa.3: Your king enters d5, and the pawn promotes: Black's opposition did not help, because it did not guard the key square.
rot.means.demos.recap.1: Before practising, the ideas of the lesson. The opposition works on a file, a diagonal and a rank, and also from afar: an odd number of squares between the kings after your move.
rot.means.demos.recap.2: Against enemy pawns, the opposition lets you go round the other king and capture them; with locked pawns, a square guarded by a pawn can decide the opposition.
rot.means.demos.recap.3: And today: the opposition is the means, and the key squares, the goal. Your turn: an attack and a defence. Before each move, ask what the goal is.
rot.means.pratica.ataque.enunciado: Play White and find the best move.
rot.means.pratica.ataque.fim: Your king reached a key square, and the pawn promoted.
rot.means.pratica.ataque.err.e3f3.1: By taking the king to f3, you keep the direct opposition, but you do not get closer to c5, d5 and e5: the win slips away.
rot.means.pratica.ataque.err.e3f3.2: The black king goes to e5, a key square, and blocks the path of your king.
rot.means.pratica.ataque.err.e3f2.1: By stepping the king back to f2, you move it away from the key squares c5, d5 and e5: the win slips away.
rot.means.pratica.ataque.err.e3f2.2: The black king goes to e5, a key square, and blocks the path of your king.
rot.means.pratica.ataque.err.e3e2.1: By stepping the king back to e2, you move it away from the key squares c5, d5 and e5: the win slips away.
rot.means.pratica.ataque.err.e3e2.2: The black king goes to e5, a key square, and blocks the path of your king.
rot.means.pratica.ataque.err.e3d2.1: By stepping the king back to d2, you move it away from the key squares c5, d5 and e5: the win slips away.
rot.means.pratica.ataque.err.e3d2.2: The black king goes to e5, a key square, and blocks the path of your king.
rot.means.pratica.ataque.err.d3d4.1: By pushing the pawn to d4 before the king, the key squares become c6, d6 and e6: the win slips away.
rot.means.pratica.ataque.err.d3d4.2: The black king goes to e6, one of the new key squares, and reaches d6 in time.
rot.means.pratica.ataque.v1.err.d3d4.1: Pushing the pawn now is too early: with it on d4, the key squares move up to c6, d6 and e6.
rot.means.pratica.ataque.v1.err.d3d4.2: The black king goes to c7, facing yours with c6 between them: Black has the opposition, and it is a draw.
rot.means.pratica.ataque.v2.err.d3d4.1: Pushing the pawn now is too early: with it on d4, the key squares move up to c6, d6 and e6.
rot.means.pratica.ataque.v2.err.d3d4.2: The black king goes to d7 and guards c6, d6 and e6: it is a draw.
rot.means.pratica.defesa.enunciado: Play Black and find the best move.
rot.means.pratica.defesa.fim: Your king guarded the key squares, and the white king did not get through.
rot.means.pratica.defesa.err.e5e4.1: By taking the king to e4, you keep the opposition, but you move away from the key squares c6, d6 and e6: the draw slips away.
rot.means.pratica.defesa.err.e5e4.2: The white king goes to c5, next to c6 and d6, two key squares, and your king is too far away to guard them.
rot.means.pratica.defesa.err.e5e6.1: By taking the king to e6, you occupy a key square, but you leave c6 unguarded: the draw slips away.
rot.means.pratica.defesa.err.e5e6.2: The white king goes to c5, next to c6 and d6, two key squares, and the black king can no longer stop the win.
rot.means.pratica.defesa.err.e5f5.1: By taking the king to f5, you move away from the key squares c6, d6 and e6: the draw slips away.
rot.means.pratica.defesa.err.e5f5.2: The white king goes to d5, next to c6, d6 and e6, and your king arrives too late.
rot.means.pratica.defesa.err.e5f6.1: By taking the king to f6, you move away from c6 and d6: the draw slips away.
rot.means.pratica.defesa.err.e5f6.2: The white king goes to d5, next to c6, d6 and e6, and your king arrives too late.
rot.means.pratica.defesa.err.e5f4.1: By taking the king to f4, you move away from the key squares c6, d6 and e6: the draw slips away.
rot.means.pratica.defesa.err.e5f4.2: The white king goes to c5, next to c6 and d6, and your king, on f4, arrives too late to guard them.
rot.means.pratica.ataque.v3.err.d3d4.1: Pushing the pawn now is too early: with it on d4, the key squares move up to c6, d6 and e6.
rot.means.pratica.ataque.v3.err.d3d4.2: The black king goes to c6, one of the new key squares, and stands in front of your king.
rot.means.pratica.ataque.v4.err.d3d4.1: Pushing the pawn now is too early: with it on d4, the key squares move up to c6, d6 and e6.
rot.means.pratica.ataque.v4.err.d3d4.2: The black king goes to d6, one of the new key squares, and blocks your king's way.
rot.means.pratica.ataque.v5.err.d3d4.1: Pushing the pawn now is too early: with it on d4, the key squares move up to c6, d6 and e6.
rot.means.pratica.ataque.v5.err.d3d4.2: The black king goes to e7, facing yours with e6 between them: Black has the opposition, and it is a draw.
rot.means.pratica.ataque.v6.err.d4d5.1: Pushing the pawn now is too early: your king is not in front of it yet, and the key squares move up to c7, d7 and e7.
rot.means.pratica.ataque.v6.err.d4d5.2: The black king goes to c7, one of the pawn's key squares, and blocks your king's way.
rot.means.pratica.ataque.v7.err.d4d5.1: Pushing the pawn now is too early: your king is not in front of it yet, and the key squares move up to c7, d7 and e7.
rot.means.pratica.ataque.v7.err.d4d5.2: The black king goes to d7, one of the pawn's key squares, and blocks your king's way.
rot.means.pratica.defesa.v1.err.d6e6.1: By taking the king to e6, you leave c6 unguarded: the draw slips away.
rot.means.pratica.defesa.v1.err.d6e6.2: The white king goes to c5, next to c6, the key square your king left unguarded.
rot.means.pratica.defesa.v2.err.d5e4.1: By taking the king to e4, you attack the pawn, but you move away from the key squares c6, d6 and e6: the draw slips away.
rot.means.pratica.defesa.v2.err.d5e4.2: The white king goes to c4, protects the pawn and heads for c6 and d6, which your king cannot reach.
rot.means.pratica.ataque.v7.err.e5d5.1: By taking the king to d5, you stand in front of your own pawn, and Black holds the opposition: the win slips away.
rot.means.pratica.ataque.v7.err.e5d5.2: The black king goes to d7, facing yours with d6 between them: Black has the opposition, and it is a draw.
rot.means.pratica.defesa.v1.err.d6d7.1: By taking the king to d7, you guard all three key squares, but you hand the opposition to White: the draw slips away.
rot.means.pratica.defesa.v1.err.d6d7.2: The white king goes to d5, facing yours with d6 between them: White has the opposition, and your king must give way.
